messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Spanish, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Nel | “in the middle of” – locative prepositional phrase introducing the position | Spanish form: **En el** (preposition + definite article, masc. sg.). Back‑translation check: “in the”. | | mezzo | The exact middle point of a journey | Spanish form: **medio** (noun/adjective, masc. sg., singular). Back‑translation check: “middle”. | | del | Genitive marker linking *cammin* to *vita* | Spanish form: **del** (contraction of *de* + *el*, preposition + definite article, masc. sg.). Back‑translation check: “of the”. | | cammin | The path or journey being travelled | Spanish form: **camino** (noun, masc. sg.). Back‑translation check: “road”. | | di | Marks possession/association (“our life”) | Spanish form: **de** (preposition). Back‑translation check: “of”. | | nostra | Indicates that the life belongs to the speaker and companions | Spanish form: **nuestra** (possessive adjective, fem. sg.). Back‑translation check: “our”. | | vita | The span of existence of the speaker and companions | Spanish form: **vida** (noun, fem. sg.). Back‑translation check: “life”. | | mi | The speaker as the experiencer of the action | Spanish form: **me** (reflexive clitic, accusative). Back‑translation check: “myself”. | | ritrovai | “I found myself” – self‑locating action | Spanish form: **encontré** (verb, 1st person singular preterite of *encontrar*). Back‑translation check: “found”. | | per | Introduces the spatial domain of the finding | Spanish form: **en** (preposition). Back‑translation check: “in”. | | una | Marks the noun *selva* as non‑specific | Spanish form: **una** (indefinite article, fem. sg.). Back‑translation check: “a”. | | selva | A forest, the dark environment | Spanish form: **selva** (noun, fem. sg.). Back‑translation check: “wood”. | | oscura | Qualifies *selva* as lacking light | Spanish form: **oscura** (adjective, fem. sg., agrees with *selva*). Back‑translation check: “dark”. | | ché | Introduces the causal clause | Spanish form: **porque** (conjunction). Back‑translation check: “because”. | | la | Specifies the particular *via* | Spanish form: **la** (definite article, fem. sg.). Back‑translation check: “the”. | | diritta | Describes the *via* as the correct/straight one | Spanish form: **recta** (adjective, fem. sg., agrees with *via*). Back‑translation check: “right”. | | via | The correct path that should be followed | Spanish form: **vía** (noun, fem. sg.). Back‑translation check: “way”. | | era | Copular verb indicating a past state | Spanish form: **estaba** (verb, 3rd person singular imperfect of *estar*). Back‑translation check: “was”. | | smarrita | State of being lost; the way is not found | Spanish form: **perdida** (adjective, fem. sg., past participle of *perder*). Back‑translation check: “lost”. |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 1: En el medio del camino de nuestra vida / A mitad del camino de nuestra vida / Sobre la mitad del sendero de nuestra vida - Line 2: Me encontré en una selva oscura / Me hallé dentro de una selva oscura / Me descubrí en una selva oscura - Line 3: porque la recta vía estaba perdida / porque la vía recta estaba perdida / porque la recta vía estaba perdida

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Spanish lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 1 Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita **Line Inventory:** - En el medio del camino de nuestra vida **Assembly Notes:** - none (phrase already forms a complete clause) **Target Text:** En el medio del camino de nuestra vida
**Source Line:** 2 mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, **Line Inventory:** - Me encontré en una selva oscura **Assembly Notes:** - added final comma to match source punctuation **Target Text:** Me encontré en una selva oscura,
**Source Line:** 3 ché la diritta via era smarrita. **Line Inventory:** - porque la recta vía estaba perdida **Assembly Notes:** - added final period to match source punctuation **Target Text:** porque la recta vía estaba perdida.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #: 1 Target Text: En el medio del camino de nuestra vida Back-Translation: In the middle of the road of our life Reference Translation: Midway upon the road of our life Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text:
- Line #: 2 Target Text: Me encontré en una selva oscura, Back-Translation: I found myself in a dark forest, Reference Translation: I found myself within a dark wood, Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text:
- Line #: 3 Target Text: porque la recta vía estaba perdida. Back-Translation: because the straight way was lost. Reference Translation: for the right way had been missed. Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text:
``` En el medio del camino de nuestra vida Me encontré en una selva oscura, porque la recta vía estaba perdida. ```
